clue.text: French composer's freedom restricted by returning offspring

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: something restricted by a boundary sits inside it, so the freedom word goes within the other piece
returning means the word for offspring is read backwards

parts.note: seed is an old word for offspring or descendants
lib is short for liberation, as in women's lib

explanation.surface: A French composer's liberty is curtailed by children coming home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freedom' suggests liberty in full, but only the short form lib, as in women's lib, is wanted. Léo Delibes wrote the ballet Coppélia.
explanation.definitionFit: Léo Delibes was a nineteenth-century French composer of ballets and operas such as Lakmé.

clue.text: Take off from party with maximum volume

parts.note: a do is British informal speech for a party
ff, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud playing

explanation.surface: Leaving a loud party.
explanation.definitionFit: To doff a hat is to remove it, a synonym of taking a garment off.

clue.text: Frenchwoman's distant, a bit of a cow, perhaps

definitions.meaning: in a French woman's speech the word for far away is used

definitions.text: a bit of a cow, perhaps
definitions.meaning: a cut of meat from the back of an animal such as a cow

explanation.surface: A French lady keeps her distance, being rather cowlike.
explanation.definitionFit: Loin is French for far, and in English a loin is a cut of meat from an animal's back.

clue.text: Very hot in Spain, the poor young socialite's overcome

indicators.note: overcome, in a down clue, suggests the pieces turned over so the whole run reads upwards

parts.note: el is the Spanish definite article
bad means poor in quality
a deb, debutante, is a young woman entering society; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: In Spain a struggling young society girl is overwhelmed by the heat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overcome' turns ELBADDEB around as a whole, reading upwards in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for sexually attractive: someone very hot is a desirable bedfellow.

clue.text: Eastern mystic's morning in the Belgravia area

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', linking definition and wordplay

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: SW1 is the London postcode district covering Belgravia, with the 1 read as I
am, ante meridiem, means morning

explanation.surface: An Eastern holy man spends his mornings in a smart London district.
explanation.walkthrough: Belgravia is an expensive district of London whose postcode is SW1; the figure 1 serves as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A swami is a Hindu religious teacher, a mystic of the East.

clue.text: Group of schoolchildren stumped by paper

parts.note: ST is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for stumped, a way of being out
a ream is a quantity of paper, 500 sheets

explanation.surface: A class of pupils is baffled by a written paper.
explanation.definitionFit: In British schools a stream is a group of pupils of similar ability taught together.

clue.text: Model having shoots

definitions.meaning: the famous 1960s fashion model known for her slender build
full of slender shoots or twigs

explanation.definitionFit: Twiggy was a celebrated British fashion model, and twiggy also describes a plant thick with shoots.

clue.text: Old pet, heard outside, is set free

parts.note: ex means former, so old

indicators.note: outside means wrapped around another piece

parts.note: a case is heard, or tried, in court
a cat is a household pet

explanation.surface: A former pet, listened to from outdoors, is let loose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard' looks like a sound-alike signal, but it means judged in court.
explanation.definitionFit: To extricate someone is to free them from a difficulty or trap.

clue.text: Car goes around in gear just over bottom

parts.note: the Mini is a classic small British car
to skirt something is to go around its edge

explanation.surface: A car drives around in clothing that barely covers the backside.
explanation.definitionFit: Miniskirts are short skirts whose hems sit only a little below the backside.

clue.text: See 10
Economist, one foregoing Keynes, famed in Republican manoeuvring

parts.note: Milton Keynes is an English new town, so the word that comes before Keynes is Milton

indicators.note: manoeuvring moves the letters of the famed-in pieces around into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An economist who came before Keynes became celebrated through Republican political scheming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One foregoing Keynes' tempts a solver toward an economist preceding John Maynard Keynes; it is the town Milton Keynes. 'manoeuvring' rearranges FAMEDIN plus R into FRIEDMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Milton Friedman was the Nobel-winning American monetarist economist of the Chicago school.

clue.text: Police trap criminal with heart of gold

indicators.note: criminal suggests something wrong or bent, so these letters are mixed up
heart of selects the central letters of the word gold

explanation.surface: Cops set a crooked snare for someone with a golden heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' rearranges TRAP into PATR, and 'heart of' takes OL from gold.
explanation.definitionFit: To patrol is to police an area by moving around it on watch; both are verbs here.

clue.text: PROFIT?

parts.note: the word is printed entirely in upper case, so it has gained capital letters, while the phrase also means profit from selling assets

explanation.walkthrough: The clue is printed in capitals: the word PROFIT has literally gained capitals, and the phrase is also the financial term for profit on an asset sale.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the tax term for profit made when an investment or asset is sold for more than it cost.

clue.text: How 10's 18 25 starts abrupt current decline

definitions.meaning: Milton's epic poem opens with the rebel angels cast down from heaven
a sheer drop in a flowing river, so a waterfall

explanation.walkthrough: The references point to Milton's Paradise Lost, which begins with Satan and his followers thrown out of heaven; the answer is also Venezuela's waterfall, the world's highest.
explanation.definitionFit: Angel Falls in Venezuela is the world's highest waterfall, and the epic opens with the fallen angels.

clue.text: Whence one gets milk and a sandwich very regularly

definitions.text: Whence one gets milk and a sandwich very regularly

parts.note: a teat is the nipple that a young mammal sucks for milk
a roll is a bread roll, often filled as a sandwich

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of the word very

explanation.surface: Where an office worker gets milk and a sandwich on a regular basis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes EY from very. The whole clue also describes the trolley wheeled round offices with tea, milk and sandwiches.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea trolley is the wheeled cart from which drinks and snacks are served, milk included.

clue.text: Foul reek — old and new sewers produce it

indicators.note: foul suggests something fouled up or messed about, so the letters that follow are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bad smell comes from the drains, old and new alike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sewers' looks like drains carrying the reek, but here it means people who sew.
explanation.definitionFit: People who sew stitch fabric, and the product of their stitching is embroidery or similar handiwork.

clue.text: Starbuck's first found here, healthier and with topping

indicators.note: topping means at the top, so the first letter of with goes uppermost in this down entry

parts.note: haler is the comparative of hale, meaning healthy

explanation.surface: A coffee chain's earliest outlet appears here, healthier and with toppings.
explanation.walkthrough: Starbuck looks like the coffee chain, but he is the first mate of the Pequod in Moby-Dick, a ship that hunted whales.
explanation.definitionFit: Starbuck was first mate of the Pequod in Moby-Dick, a whaling ship, so a first mate is found on one.

clue.text: Novelist lacking close friend

indicators.note: lacking its close means the novelist's surname loses its final letter

parts.note: Kingsley or Martin Amis, both British novelists

explanation.surface: A writer has no intimate companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking close' drops the last letter of AMIS. 'Close friend' reads as one phrase, but 'close' belongs to the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Ami is the French word for a friend, often used in English crosswords.

clue.text: Garden is planted in March

indicators.note: planted in means set within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to march is to parade

explanation.surface: A garden is sown in the spring month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'March' looks like the month but is the verb, parade.
explanation.definitionFit: Paradise is the Garden of Eden, from a Persian word for an enclosed garden.

clue.text: Online paper shows amphibian

parts.note: E stands for electronic, as in e-mail, so it means online
FT is the Financial Times, a British newspaper

explanation.surface: A web newspaper features a frog-like creature.
explanation.definitionFit: An eft is a newt, particularly a young one, which is a small amphibian.

clue.text: One raising issue about letters backing the legislators

indicators.note: about means going around, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: issue means children, and a parent raises them

indicators.note: backing means the word for letters is reversed

parts.note: mail is the letters delivered by the post

explanation.surface: Someone bringing up a matter about correspondence supports the lawmakers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' suggests a topic for debate, but means offspring; 'letters' is the post rather than the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Parliament is the body of elected lawmakers, as in Britain's Westminster.

clue.text: Woman eating cheap products displays figure

indicators.note: eating means taking something inside, so one piece contains the other

parts.note: Sue is a woman's name
tat is British slang for cheap, shoddy goods

explanation.surface: A woman munching on junk shows her shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A statue is a carved or cast figure of a person.

clue.text: Borderline character with impudence remains wild

parts.note: front means cheek or brazen nerve, a sense of impudence

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so these letters run in a disordered arrangement

explanation.surface: A cheeky character on the edge leaves his remains scattered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Borderline' reads as 'nearly', but means living on a frontier; 'remains' looks like the noun yet is anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A frontiersman lives on the border of settled country, so he is a person of the borderland.

clue.text: What journalist wants — Sun to shut up

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for Sun, as in Sunday
to coop up is to confine or shut in

explanation.surface: A reporter wants the Sun newspaper to stay quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sun' looks like the British tabloid, but it is S.
explanation.definitionFit: A scoop is an exclusive story that a reporter gets before rivals.

clue.text: See 25
What one makes up for depraved sentence

parts.note: a lost soul is morally ruined, so depraved
time is a prison sentence, as in doing time

explanation.surface: Compensation for a wicked jail term.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition completes the idiom about catching up after a delay.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is to make up for delay: one hurries to recover the hours that were wasted.

clue.text: Novel that's hilarious, one getting thanks

parts.note: LOL, laugh out loud, is internet shorthand for something hilarious
I is the Roman numeral one
ta is British informal speech for thank you

explanation.surface: A book that's very funny wins someone's gratitude.
explanation.definitionFit: Lolita is the famous 1955 novel by Vladimir Nabokov.

clue.text: Complaint about jerk being an MP

indicators.note: about means around, so the complaint word wraps the jerk word

parts.note: a complaint is an illness, and polio is one
a tic is an involuntary jerk or twitch

explanation.surface: A grievance about some idiot's behaviour as a member of parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complaint' reads as a grumble, but here it is an illness. 'Jerk' suggests a fool, not a twitch.
explanation.definitionFit: A politico is a politician, and a Member of Parliament is one such.

clue.text: Filthy place was first to be knocked into shape

parts.note: a pigsty, or sty, is the proverbial dirty place
to have led is to have been in front, first in a race

explanation.surface: A dirty spot was the first thing to be tidied.
explanation.definitionFit: To style something is to shape or fashion it, as a hairdresser does.

clue.text: Stop media manipulation happening!

parts.note: PR, public relations, is the craft of managing the media
an event is something that happens, an occurrence

explanation.surface: A protest against spin doctoring as it takes place.
explanation.definitionFit: To prevent something is to stop it from happening at all.
